- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above recent peak for 3–7 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and prices are trending down, model frequently underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price decline, forecast should not drop below 1–2 standard deviations below recent low.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; smooth forecast by averaging last 7–10 days’ values if sentiment volatility >0.2.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to align with sentiment momentum direction.
